android.desc:
Kibo is an expense tracker and budget app for everyday money. Add an expense in seconds or snap the receipt, and Kibo picks the category.

Try Premium free for 7 days. Use everything, then keep the free plan or stay on Premium.

Know where your money goes
Your month on one screen: what you have spent so far, what you spent today and where the month is heading. Every expense carries its category and an image, so the list reads at a glance.

Log an expense in seconds
Type the amount and a name. Kibo suggests the category as you type: groceries, coffee, a taxi or the purchase you forgot about. If you want a different one, change it with a tap.

Save for what matters
Set a savings goal for each thing you want: a trip, a new laptop or an emergency fund. Each goal fills up as you save, shows how much is left and when you will get there at your pace.

Savings on autopilot
Pick an amount and a day, every week or every month, and Kibo adds it for you. Pause or change it whenever you like.

Your month at a glance
A calendar that marks the days you spend the most, your priciest day, your daily average and the split by category. When the month ends, you get a short recap.

Scan a receipt. Done.
Take a photo of a receipt and Kibo reads the merchant, the total and the date.

Make it yours
Nine color themes in light or dark mode, or the colors of your wallpaper.

No surprises from fixed costs
Every subscription and recurring bill in one place, with this week's charges, a heads-up before each renewal and the full charge history.

Also included
• Spaces. Keep a trip, a move or a home project apart from the month so it does not skew your numbers.
• Budgets per category, with a nudge before you go over.
• Statement import. Bring your bank's CSV and Kibo categorizes every row.
• Works offline. Entries wait on the phone and sync when you are back online.
• Widget and a Quick Settings tile to log without opening the app.
• Income. Track what comes in next to what goes out.

Privacy first
Kibo never sells your data and shows no ads. Google and a few other providers process it on our behalf to run the app, suggest categories and measure usage. Your entries are encrypted in transit, and you can delete your account from the app at any time. Details at ki-bo.com/privacy-policy.

Free and Premium
Free: 25 expenses a month, 5 receipt scans, 3 fixed expenses, 2 savings goals, 1 Space, 1 budget and the last 30 days of history.
Premium: unlimited

show_hn.title: Show HN: Kibo, AI expense tracker for Android with AI categorization

quotes.text:
Hi HN,

I’ve been working nights and weekends on my first Android app, and last week I finally launched it. It’s called Kibo, a simple, privacy-focused expense tracker that uses AI and OCR to make logging expenses less painful.

The problem I wanted to solve:
I tried a bunch of budgeting apps, but most were either slow, bloated, full of ads, or locked basic features behind subscriptions. I wanted something I’d actually use every day — fast, lightweight, and private.

What Kibo does:
 • AI suggests categories + emojis instantly from the expense name
 • OCR reads receipts and fills in transaction details automatically
 • Clean Material You design with light/dark/system themes
 • Free tier includes 20 transactions/month with unlimited custom categories
 • Secure cloud sync (end-to-end encrypted)

Tech stack:
Built with Kotlin + Jetpack Compose, Firebase for auth/storage, and MLKit for OCR. AI categorization uses a lightweight NLP model fine-tuned on category datasets.

I’d love feedback on both the UX and the technical side. How would you approach improving discoverability of a niche consumer app like this? Also open to suggestions on the architecture — right now everything runs client-side except sync.

Play Store link: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.kibo.app

Thanks for checking it out — happy to dive into the code or design decisions if anyone’s curious.
